title: Focal length vs camera position — Image Wiki

rules.rule: If near parts of a subject appear oversized relative to far parts, the camera was positioned close to the subject.
rules.evidence: Near parts oversized against far parts means a close camera, and nothing else.

rules.rule: If distant background objects appear huge behind the subject, the camera was positioned far back with a long lens.
rules.evidence: Distant buildings or hills rendered huge behind the subject means the camera was far back with a long lens.

rules.rule: If straight lines bow outward near edges, it is barrel distortion caused by a lens defect, not camera position.
rules.evidence: Bowed near the edges is barrel or pincushion, a lens defect.
